en: *Jingxing chao zhujia ji biaomu* (The Index to the Records of Various Masters on the *Jingxing chao*), compiled by the later scholar Śramaṇa Jièyuè;
revised record of the ten fascicles of the *Jingxing chao ji* (the name of the original compiler is unknown).
This one work, the *Shōsho* (Commentary on the Essentials), was composed by the Vinaya Master Chiren of Kōmyō-ji Temple in the Tang capital of Jingzhao;
it marks the beginning of the various schools of commentary and is thus said to stand outside the so-called "sixty houses."
The *Xingxi chao* cites the twenty-one-fascicle *Yuanji*.
This one work was composed by Vinaya Master Lingche of Yunmen Temple in Kuaiji during the Tang dynasty;
it is likewise included among the sixty schools.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi* (The Record of the *Hsing-shih-ch'ao*; the name of the author and the number of fascicles have not yet been verified).
One volume, composed by the Vinaya Master Daci of Ximing Monastery in the capital of Tang China.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi* (as above).

The first work, *Xingshicha Dangyangji* (Record of the Practice Manual from Dangyang), was composed by Vinaya Master Hengjing (also read as Hongjing) of Longxing Temple during the Tang dynasty; its number of fascicles is unknown.
The second work was composed by Vinaya Master Tansheng of Jingzhou during the Tang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi* (The Record of the *Hsing-shih-ch'ao*; name of the recorder and number of fascicles unknown).
One volume, composed by Vinaya Master Rong-ji of Fu-zhou during the Tang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi* (as above).
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Daoshen of Quanzhou during the Tang Dynasty;
it is titled *Xingshichao Xiheji* (the number of fascicles has not been verified).
The following work was composed by Vinaya Master Chongfu of Huzhou during the Tang Dynasty.
*Commentary on the *Xing-shi chao* (author’s name and number of fascicles unknown).
One volume, compiled by Vinaya Master Linghe of Chongsheng Temple during the Tang Dynasty.
*Commentary on the Xing-shi chao* (as above).
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Zhikai of Huzhou during the Tang Dynasty.
*Xingshichao ji* (as above).
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Falin of Huzhou during the Tang Dynasty.
*Hángshìchāojì* (Record of the *Hángshìchāo*), ten fascicles (the author’s name is unknown).
The above work, one set, was composed by Vinaya Master Dàohéng of Kāiyuán Monastery in Sūzhōu during the Táng dynasty.
*Hángshìchāojīngǔjì* (Ancient and Modern Records of the *Hángshìchāo*), ten fascicles.
The first work, in ten fascicles, titled *Xingshichao Yuanchengji* (Record of the Perfect Realization of the *Xingshichao*), was composed by the Tang dynasty Vinaya Master Zhiming.
The second work, in ten fascicles, was composed by the Tang dynasty Vinaya Master Zhichan.
*Fuxing xingshi chao Fuyang ji*, ten fascicles.
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Fayan of Hangzhou during the Tang dynasty.
*Xingshi chao Zhixing ji* (the number of fascicles has not yet been verified).

The above one work, in ten fascicles, titled *Xingshichao Fupian Ji* (Record of the Supplementary Chapters to the *Xingshichao*), was composed by Vinaya Master Faxing of Suzhou during the Tang Dynasty.
The following one work, [in ten fascicles], was composed by Vinaya Master Xuanyan of Fahua Temple in Yuezhou during the Tang Dynasty.
*Fazheng ji* (Record for Elucidating the Correct) in ten fascicles;
this one work was composed by the Vinaya Master Jueyin of Kaiyuan Temple in Kuaiji during the Tang Dynasty.
*Zhongzhong ji* (Record of the Middle Way) in six fascicles on the *Xingshi chao*.
The above work, one fascicle, was composed by Vinaya Master Yixuan (alternatively Chao) of Xingning Temple in Changzhou during the Tang Dynasty;
it is titled *Xingshichaohuizhengji* (alternatively *Maoji*; the number of fascicles is unknown).
The following work, one fascicle, was composed by Vinaya Master Zhixiang of the Tang Dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao Ku-chin-chüeh* (also titled *Tz'u-ho-chi*), ten fascicles.
This work, comprising one volume, was composed by Vinaya Master Lang-jan of Chao-yin Monastery in Runzhou during the Tang dynasty.

The above one work, in six fascicles, titled *Xingshichao Ji* (Record of the *Xingshichao*;
the title of the record has not been verified), was composed by Vinaya Master Weiqian of Runzhou during the Tang dynasty.
The following one work was composed by Vinaya Master Huichao of the Tang dynasty.
*Xingshichao Ji* (Record of the *Xingshichao*), seven fascicles (one version says six fascicles; the author of the record has not been identified).
The above work, one set, was composed by Vinaya Master Bianchang of Hangzhou during the Tang dynasty.
*Xingshichao Lingshan Ji* (Record of the *Xingshichao* from Mount Ling), [fascicle count not yet determined].
The above work, in fourteen fascicles, was composed by Vinaya Master Yiwēi of Chándìng Monastery in the Western Capital (Cháng'ān) during the Táng dynasty;
it is titled *Qīfēnlǜ chāo pī* (also known as *Huáyán jì*).
The following work, [in fourteen fascicles], was composed by Vinaya Master Dàjué of Huá-yán Monastery in Hángzhōu during the Táng dynasty.
*Xingshi chao souxuan lu* (The Search for the Profound Record of the *Xingshi chao*), twenty fascicles:
this work, comprising one volume, was composed by the Great Master Zhìhóng of Chángshòu at Shuānglín Monastery in Wújùn during the Táng dynasty.
*Xingshi chao shunzheng ji* (The Record of Accordance with Correctness on the *Xingshi chao*), ten fascicles.
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Shengong of Huizhao Monastery in Yangzhou during the Tang Dynasty.
The *Xingshichao Tongxuanji* (number of fascicles unverified) was composed by Vinaya Master Changjin of Tongxuan Monastery during the Tang Dynasty.
*Hanshōki* (Record of the *Hanshō*), six fascicles (the name of the record is unexamined).
One set, composed by the Tang dynasty Vinaya Master Kanso.
*Hanshōki*, four fascicles (the name of the record is unknown).
The above work, one volume, was composed by Vinaya Master Tanqing of the Tang dynasty:
*Xingshichao Xianzong ji* (the number of fascicles has not been verified).
The above work, one volume, was composed by Vinaya Master Tanqing of Weiyu Temple during the Tang dynasty.
*Xingshichao Jiyiji* (also known as *Houtangji*), twenty fascicles.
This work, comprising one volume, was composed by Vinaya Master Qingche of Longxing Temple in Zhongling during the Tang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi* (The Record of the *Hsing-shih-ch'ao*; the name of the record and its volume count have not been verified).
This one work was composed by the Vinaya Master Kuang-hsiung of the Tang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi*, ten volumes (the name of the record has not been verified).
The first work, in ten fascicles, titled *Xingshichao Xianzhengji* (An Elucidation and Rectification of the *Xingshichao*), was composed by the Vinaya Master Zhicui of the Tang dynasty.
The second work, in ten fascicles, was composed by the Great Master Fabao, named Xuanchang, of Zongchi Monastery.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi-tsung-chi* (number of fascicles not yet verified).
One volume, composed by Vinaya Master Tsung-chih of Ch’ang-an during the Tang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi* (name and number of fascicles of this commentary not yet verified).
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master De-yuan of Xiu Prefecture during the Tang Dynasty.
*Xing-shi-chao-ji* (as noted above).
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Dan-fu of Kaiyuan Temple in Yue Prefecture during the Tang Dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi* (as above).
The above one work was composed by Vinaya Master Chung-p’ing of Hu-chou during the T’ang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch’ao chi-yao chi*, twelve fascicles.
The above work, in one section, was composed by Vinaya Master Huize of Ximing Monastery during the Later Liang dynasty.
*Xingshichao Yiji* (Record of the Meaning of the *Xingshichao*), five fascicles;
the above work, in one section, was composed by Vinaya Master Yuanbiao of Dashi Monastery in Yuezhou during the Later Liang dynasty.
*Changshui Ji* on the *Xingshi Chao* (the number of fascicles has not been verified).
This one work was composed by Vinaya Master Quanli of Xiuzhou during the Later Liang dynasty.
*Shangyuan Ji* on the *Xingshi Chao* (as above).
The above one volume was composed by Vinaya Master Huimi of the Later Liang.
*Xingshichao Guijingji* (as noted above).
The above one volume was composed by Vinaya Master Huiyou of the Later Liang.
*Jianzheng ji* (Abridged and Corrected Record) of the *Xingshi chao*, twenty fascicles.
This work, comprising one volume, was composed by Vinaya Master Jingxiao of Zhenshen Baota Temple in Hangzhou during the Later Tang dynasty.
It is a record of the "Chapter on the Four Fruits of Observance and Transgression" from the *Xingshi chao* (fascicle count not yet verified).
The above work, one fascicle, was composed by Vinaya Master Wuwai of Hangzhou during the Later Tang dynasty.
*Xingshichao Shoujingji* (as listed above).
The above work, one fascicle, was composed by Vinaya Master Deyin of Wuzhou during the Later Tang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chih-chi chi* (Record of the Index to the *Hsing-shih-ch'ao*), five fascicles.
The above work, one set, was composed by Vinaya Master Chüeh-chao of Hang-chou during the Later T'ang dynasty.
*Hsing-shih-ch'ao chi-i chi* (Record of the Collected Meanings of the *Hsing-shih-ch'ao*) [fascicle count not yet verified].
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Qingyan of Hongzhou during the Later Tang dynasty.
The phonetic glosses for the commentary are as [listed] above.
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Chongyi of Yuezhou during the Later Tang dynasty.
*Xingshichao ji* (the name of the author and the number of fascicles have not yet been verified);
one volume, composed by Master Lidu of the Later Tang.
*Xingshichao zenghui ji*, twenty fascicles.
The aforementioned one work, the *Xingshichao Shiyiji* (Supplementary Records to the *Xingshichao*) in three fascicles,
was composed by Dharma Master Huijue of Qianfo Monastery in Qiantang,
Han. The aforementioned one work, [the *Xingshichao Shiyiji*], was composed by Vinaya Master Chuyun of Hangzhou, Song.
*Xingshi chao jiji ji* (Collected Explanations of the *Xingshi chao*), twelve fascicles.
The aforementioned work was composed by the Vinaya Master Puzhi of Yuezhou during the Song dynasty.
*Xingshi chao yinyi zhigui* (The Essential Guide to the Phonology and Meaning of the *Xingshi chao*), three fascicles.

The above work, in ten fascicles, titled *Xingshichao Zhengyanji* (Record of Correct Words on the *Xingshichao*), was composed by Dharma Master Tōnghuì of Tiānshòu Monastery in Jīngzhào during the Song Dynasty. The following work,
in one fascicle, was composed by Vinaya Master Déming of Shèngzhōu during the Song Dynasty.
*Hanshi chao yi yuan ji* (Record of the Garden of Meanings for the *Hanshi chao*), seven fascicles;
the aforementioned work was composed by Vinaya Master Zewu of Hangzhou during the Song dynasty.
*Hanshi chao hui zheng ji* (Record for Rectifying the *Hanshi chao*), thirteen (one version says two) fascicles.
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Yunkan of Bodhi Temple in Qiantang, Song Dynasty.
*Xingshi chao jianzheng ji* (number of fascicles unknown).
The above work was composed by Vinaya Master Wenbo of Wenzhou, Song Dynasty.
*Xingshichao Zizhiji*, sixteen fascicles (alternatively, two fascicles).
This work, comprising one volume, was composed by the Vinaya Master Dazhi Yuanzhao of Lingzhi Chongfu Monastery during the Song dynasty.
